subject: Senior Inference Engineer — assessment scope & debrief playbook
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@nimbushealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Candidate: Sara Lim — availability + scope alignment

Hi Aditya, Marissa, Laura —

Hope you’re well. We’ve got Sara Lim on deck for the Senior Inference Engineer loop next Wednesday (9/22). Sara’s profile looks strong on productionizing LLMs and infra optimizations — attaching her resume (sara_lim_resume.pdf). Before we finalize the schedule, the hiring team asked for a quick alignment on the assessment scope and debrief expectations so we evaluate consistently across interviewers.

Quick context: Sara has ~6 years building retrieval + serving pipelines and some recent work on quantization/latency tuning. Nimbus cares most about: throughput/latency tradeoffs, safe rollout strategies, and system-level debugging.

Can you confirm:
- Which two areas we want to prioritize during the loop (system design, model-runtime troubleshooting, or infra/batch sizing)?
- Leveling anchor: are we assessing strong senior (IC4) or leaning toward staff (IC5) expectations around ownership and cross-team influence?
- Debrief: do we want a scored rubric (1–4) vs narrative + hire/no-hire recommendation?

We’re aiming to lock the interviewers and invite by EOD today. Proposed window: 9/22, 10:00–13:00 PT (3x 45-min interviews + 30-min buffer).

Thanks — I can adjust calendar once you confirm.

—Lena
Nimbus Health — Talent

Attachment: sara_lim_resume.pdf (application/pdf, 320KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate: Sara Lim — availability + scope alignment

Thanks Lena — forwarding to the interviewing panel for quick alignment.

High level from my side (proposed):
- Focus areas: (1) System design for high-throughput LLM inference at scale (service architecture, autoscaling, routing/fallbacks), (2) Practical runtime debugging and latency investigations (profiling, KV cache, quantization impacts).
- Leveling anchor: treat this as Senior (IC4) bar. We expect clear ownership examples and demonstrable impact on production systems; staff (IC5) signals are a plus but not required. If candidate shows cross-org influence and project strategy, call out as +.
- Debrief format: please use the attached one-page debrief template (short rubric + 3-line recommendation). We want consistent numeric scoring across three axes: Technical breadth, System rigor, Ownership & Communication. Narrative comments are required for any 1 or 4 scores.

Interviewer assignments (proposed):
- Marissa: Service architecture + autoscaling (45m) — ownership examples + tradeoffs.
- Karthik: Runtime/latency debugging (45m) — profiling, KV cache, quantization experiments.
- Laura: Product+operational judgement (45m) — rollouts, monitoring, incident response.

Please reply with any objections by EOD; if silent I’ll accept as confirmed and Lena — please send invites for 9/22 10:00–13:00 PT.

Two quick notes:
- Keep the system design question concrete — expect a 10–15m deep-dive on a single pipeline decision rather than broad whiteboarding.
- We’ll reserve 20 min for a rapid sync after the loop for debriefers to fill the rubric.

Thanks,
Aditya
Sr. PM, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Sep 19, 2027 at 19:05, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> High level from my side (proposed):
> - Focus areas: (1) System design for high-throughput LLM inference at scale (service architecture, autoscaling, routing/fallbacks), (2) Practical runtime debugging and latency investigations (profiling, KV cache, quantization impacts).
> - Leveling anchor: treat this as Senior (IC4) bar. We expect clear ownership examples and demonstrable impact on production systems; staff (IC5) signals are a plus but not required.

Thanks — that makes sense. Two clarifying Qs:
1) For the runtime debugging slot (Karthik) — do we want to surface expectations around hands-on profiling (e.g., interpreting perf traces, memory vs compute bottlenecks) vs architectural mitigations (e.g., sharding KV cache)? I can tailor the question accordingly.
2) For ownership scoring: do we prefer to weight product/ops impact higher for this role (50/50 technical vs operational) or keep a straight 1/3 split across the three axes?

My inclination: make the runtime slot primarily hands-on (profiling & mitigation) — we should see a real troubleshooting thought process. For weighting — I’d prefer a slight tilt toward operational impact for this role (40% technical breadth, 40% system rigor, 20% ownership) but I’m fine with the panel agreeing to uniform weighting if people prefer.

I’ll hold the proposed time on my calendar pending confirmation.

—Laura
Hiring Manager, Inference Services
Redwood Inference

- I made the calendar invite for 9/22 10:00–13:00 PT and included the loop plan + links. Invite link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc1234_senior-loop
- Attached a one-page debrief template (debrief_template.md). Please use the numeric rubric and keep notes to 2–3 bullets per axis — that helps hiring committee read-through.
- I’ll own the 20-min post-loop sync and will capture a single hire/reject + short justification. If anyone needs extra time for notes, ping me and I’ll extend the buffer.

Also — small ask for the runtime slot: if you can prep one specific artifact or perf trace example to show the candidate (e.g., a simple tail-latency spike trace), that will make the troubleshooting exercise concrete and fair. I’ll upload a sanitized trace to Drive and share before the loop.
